parsed.explanation: Private conduct is legal, but public same-sex expression carries 6 months-2 years' imprisonment and is the documented lever for arrests on false accusations plus law-enforcement mistreatment/torture of LGBTQ people. No legal gender recognition, so visitors are assessed against issued documents; no anti-discrimination protection in health, employment, education or services; entrenched discrimination and concealment. No trans-specific border, facility, custody or violence record is documented, so the rating extrapolates from the enforced public-morals regime, security-force abuse context, and absence of recourse, not from silence as safety.

entry_documents.exposure: No legal gender recognition; officials assess visitor against documents as issued, creating mismatch exposure.
entry_documents.interaction: Document mismatch can trigger public-morals scrutiny, detention and custody abuse documented for LGBTQ people.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Documented arrests on false same-sex accusations and mistreatment/torture of LGBTQ people by law enforcement; general 2012 record of torture and harsh prisons.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: Arrest under Art.85 leads into a custody system with documented impunity for security-force abuse.

care_services.exposure: Entrenched discrimination in healthcare, education and employment documented for LGBT people collectively; no trans-specific care rule documented.
care_services.protection: No anti-discrimination law in health or services; sensitive-data law names sexual orientation only, not gender identity.
care_services.interaction: Outing in care risks discrimination and disclosure with no documented remedy.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: Art.85 punishes public same-sex expression as attack on public morals, heavier than other morals offences; SOGI framed as taboo/imported contrary to values.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: Private consensual same-sex activity is legal; 2012 report recorded no arrests under provisions.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Vague public-morals framing enables discretionary enforcement against visible gender nonconformity.

minors_guardians.exposure: Public-morals penalty rises to 2-5 years where one participant is a child; no trans-traveller family rule documented.
minors_guardians.interaction: Travelling with a minor increases visibility and investigation risk if relationship/identity is read as same-sex under birth-sex status.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: Entrenched societal discrimination, concealment to avoid it, relationship described as dangerous; 2023 report recorded no violence reports, ambiguity unresolved.
street_violence_police_response.protection: No known LGBTQ-rights organisations documented; no recourse documented.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Concealment norm and police mistreatment reduce likelihood police protect a trans visitor.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: No anti-discrimination or hate-crime recourse documented; UPR SOGI recommendations and UN statement not shown operating.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Data-protection Art.17 bars sensitive-data processing risking discrimination for sexual orientation only.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Paper commitments do not offset documented enforcement and discrimination without operating remedies.

anchor_checks.comparison: Similar or lower: both have birth-sex/document mismatch exposure, imprisonment possible, and custody assault risk with slow/no remedy. This dossier lacks a documented birth-sex prison-placement rule, but documented law-enforcement torture and a 2-year morals penalty keep it near this tier rather than above it.

Lower than 0.35-B: that anchor has stops, confiscation, fines and hours-long detention rarely becoming imprisonment. Here the statute prescribes up to 2 years, arrests and torture/mistreatment by police are documented, and no functioning complaint remedy is shown.

Materially lower: 0.55-B involves discretionary secondary screening, refused entry and slow appeal without custodial abuse. This dossier adds criminal imprisonment, documented police torture, entrenched discrimination and total absence of anti-discrimination recourse.

parsed.synthesis: Combined regime: no subnational variation documented. Exposure chain is document mismatch/visibility -> public-morals arrest -> detention where security-force torture and impunity are documented, plus everyday discrimination in services with no legal remedy. Protection is narrow: private conduct legal and an old 2012 no-arrest record, neither shown current or trans-specific. Interaction of criminal framing, taboo/imported framing, and police abuse makes outing potentially custodial. Thin trans-specific data resolves toward structural risk, not midpoint.
